documents.unit: Thomas Jefferson University (student policy handbook, academic policies)
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) Policy)
documents.summary: A short university-wide handbook policy (created 2023) that leaves the decision on generative AI to faculty, to be recorded in each course syllabus as either permitted (with citation) or restricted. Students own their work and must acknowledge AI use, embedded assistive tools remain usable unless prohibited, and violations fall under the Academic Integrity Policy.
documents.stance_why: The policy says GAI use "is under the purview of the faculty ... and is documented in the course syllabus" and offers two categories, "Permitted Use of GAI" and "Restricted Use of GAI"; it sets no default itself, so it delegates and lists these two as tiers.

units.why: The Purpose section says the policy "defines the acceptable use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) in academic courses", an institution-level statement of purpose and scope, so P56 fits better than P61 (which is about definitions).
units.anchor: defines the acceptable use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) in academic courses

units.why: The same sentence says the policy "identifies related policies, documents, guidelines and best-practices", a cross-reference to other guidance. No type covers pointers, so P56 is nearest, with a fit note.
units.anchor: identifies related policies, documents, guidelines and best-practices
units.fit_note: It only says the policy identifies related documents; it states no principles.

units.why: The definition calls academic integrity "vital to advancing a culture of fairness, trust and respect", grounding AI rules in fairness and community honesty rather than skill-building, so P95 rather than P41.
units.anchor: vital to advancing a culture of fairness, trust and respect

units.why: "All members of the University community must ... be honest in their own work, words and ideas" binds everyone to honest authorship of their own work, which is P29.
units.anchor: be honest in their own work, words and ideas

units.why: "The use of GAI at Thomas Jefferson University must adhere to the standards set forth in this policy found in the Academic Integrity Policy" ties GAI use to an existing university policy, so P77 rather than P36 (it classifies nothing as misconduct).
units.anchor: The use of GAI at Thomas Jefferson University must adhere to the standards

units.why: The Assistive AI definition says embedded-AI tools "are permissible when an individual creates content and applies the tool to refine their work", exempting routine features such as spelling and search, which is P100.
units.anchor: Unless specifically prohibited, use of these tools is permissible

units.why: The same definition conditions the exemption on the individual who "creates content and applies the tool to refine their work", keeping the student as author. P32 is nearest but it is a general principle, hence the fit note.
units.anchor: when an individual creates content and applies the tool to refine their work
units.fit_note: The condition is attached to the assistive-tool exemption, not a general rule that students stay the primary thinker.

units.why: The Course Syllabus definition says it "includes select policies; including the use of GAI in coursework", locating the AI rule in the syllabus, which is P09, though it is phrased as a definition rather than an instruction.
units.anchor: policies; including the use of GAI in coursework
units.fit_note: Framed as a definition of the syllabus, not an explicit instruction to include an AI statement.

units.why: The definition describes GAI as "a set of tools/algorithms capable of generating original text, images, audio, video, and computer code", fixing what the policy covers, so P61.
units.anchor: a set of tools/algorithms capable of generating original text, images, audio, video, and computer code

units.why: "Permitted Use of GAI: Authorizes use of GAI with appropriate citation in a specifically identified course and/or assignment" names one of two categories of use, so P05 (named categories) rather than P04 (who decides).
units.anchor: Authorizes use of GAI with appropriate citation in a specifically identified course and/or assignment
units.fit_note: Only two categories, not several levels.

units.why: "Restricted Use of GAI: Identifies limits around or prohibits the use of GAI in an identified course and/or assignment" names the second category, approved by department or college as appropriate; P05 for the same reason.
units.anchor: Identifies limits around or prohibits the use of GAI in an identified course and/or assignment
units.fit_note: Only two categories, not several levels.

units.why: "The use of ... GAI tools in a course is under the purview of the faculty" hands the decision to faculty within department, college and University policies, so P04.
units.anchor: is under the purview of the faculty in accordance with department, college and University policies

units.why: The same sentence says the use "is documented in the course syllabus", requiring the rule to be written down in the syllabus; P09.
units.anchor: is documented in the course syllabus

units.why: "Use of GAI beyond the approved instance ... is a violation of academic integrity" classifies unapproved use as misconduct handled under integrity rules, which is P36.
units.anchor: is a violation of academic integrity

units.why: The same sentence makes use "lacking appropriate citation" a violation, so failure to cite is itself the violation, which is P28 (not P24, which is the duty to disclose, coded separately).
units.anchor: lacking appropriate citation is a violation of academic integrity

units.why: "The Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) Policy elaborates on the use of GAI in the University Academic Integrity Policy" states how this policy relates to the integrity policy; P77 is nearest, with a fit note.
units.anchor: elaborates on the use of GAI in the University Academic Integrity Policy
units.fit_note: Describes the policy as an elaboration of the integrity policy rather than a compliance duty.

units.why: The Scope section says the policy is "applicable to all Thomas Jefferson University academic coursework both on-campus and online", setting what it covers, which is P61.
units.anchor: applicable to all Thomas Jefferson University academic coursework both on-campus and online

units.why: "The acceptable use of AI tools in a course is stated in the course syllabus" requires each course to state its AI rule in the syllabus, which is P09.
units.anchor: The acceptable use of AI tools in a course is stated in the course syllabus

units.why: The syllabus statement "may reflect: a.) Permitted Use of GAI b.) Restricted Use of GAI", two named categories, so P05.
units.anchor: may reflect: a.) Permitted Use of GAI b.) Restricted Use of GAI

units.why: Where GAI is permitted the student will "accept responsibility as owner of their work submitted", including the validity of content, so P29 (accountability for what is submitted).
units.anchor: accept responsibility as owner of their work submitted

units.why: Students must "appropriately acknowledge the use of GAI that contributed to their work even if that information is not in their final submission", a duty to disclose permitted use, so P24.
units.anchor: appropriately acknowledge the use of GAI that contributed to their work

units.why: In restricted or prohibited courses "these may be used unless specifically prohibited": embedded assistive tools stay usable, which is P100.
units.anchor: these may be used unless specifically prohibited

units.why: "the instructor will identify in writing those instances, if any, where the technology may be used" obliges instructors to list allowed uses under a restricted rule. P09 is the nearest communication type, with a fit note.
units.anchor: the instructor will identify in writing those instances, if any,
units.fit_note: Requires exceptions to a restriction to be listed in writing, not that every syllabus carries an AI statement.

units.why: "In all instances, students must adhere to the Academic Integrity Policy of the University which includes the use of GAI" binds students to the integrity policy in every course; P77.
units.anchor: students must adhere to the Academic Integrity Policy of the University

units.why: "All violations are subject to the sanctions identified in this policy" says sanctions apply but names none, so it is misconduct handling (P36), not concrete penalties (P37).
units.anchor: All violations are subject to the sanctions identified in this policy

units.why: "Created: 2023" states when the policy was made, an adoption date, so P84 fits, though no process or body is described.
units.anchor: Created: 2023
units.fit_note: Gives only a creation year, no process or body.

notes: Only one included document. Saved text includes navigation, which was skipped. The policy has no default rule or penalties; sanctions sit in the separate Academic Integrity Policy.
